title: API Foundations
description: Learn JavaScript fundamentals, browser interaction, and asynchronous local data by building toward a Campus Event Explorer.

modules.title: HTTP and API Contracts
modules.purpose: Build a concrete mental model of HTTP requests and responses before writing server routes.
learningObjectives: Trace client-server request/response exchanges.
Choose HTTP methods and interpret status codes.
Read headers and JSON message bodies.
Describe a small stable API contract.
guidedExercises: Trace request and response records line by line.
Choose methods and statuses for concrete resource operations.
Inspect JSON bodies separately from HTTP metadata.

sections.title: HTTP Requests and Responses
sections.summary: Understand the protocol and data contract an API exposes before implementing a server.

topics.title: API Requests, Responses, and Endpoints
topics.summary: Trace an HTTP exchange and identify the client, server, method, URL, endpoint, request, and response.
learningGoals: Distinguish client and server responsibilities in an API exchange.
Read a URL and identify the endpoint being requested.
Explain how one request produces one response.

topics.title: HTTP Methods, Status Codes, and Headers
topics.summary: Choose appropriate HTTP methods, interpret common status codes, and read the metadata carried by headers.
learningGoals: Use GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE according to the operation being requested.
Interpret common 2xx, 4xx, and 5xx status codes.
Explain how request and response headers carry metadata.

topics.title: JSON Bodies and API Contracts
topics.summary: Read and build JSON request and response bodies while keeping field names and data shapes predictable.
learningGoals: Distinguish HTTP metadata from a JSON message body.
Design a small predictable JSON resource shape.
Explain why clients depend on stable response contracts.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Interpret one complete API response record with JavaScript.

topics.title: Build an API Response Inspector
topics.summary: Create a Node.js program that interprets a small HTTP-response record and prints a useful summary.
learningGoals: Represent response metadata with a JavaScript object.
Interpret status, headers, and JSON body together.
Produce a readable API-response summary.

projectBrief.scenario: A frontend team needs a tiny diagnostic utility for understanding the responses returned by a campus events service.
projectBrief.role: JavaScript developer responsible for interpreting a small API response contract.
projectBrief.workspace: A local Node.js workspace with server.js, package.json, terminal access, and deterministic localhost HTTP requests. Express is provided by the course environment; learners do not install packages or call public APIs.
projectBrief.deliverable: A command-line API Response Inspector that reports method, endpoint, status category, content type, and a useful body summary.
requirements: Use JavaScript objects, conditionals, functions, and JSON concepts already learned in JavaScript Foundations.
Treat method, endpoint, status, headers, and body as separate responsibilities.
Build cumulatively: every step keeps the complete previous solution.
Do not make external network requests.

stepLadder.title: Store the response record
stepLadder.requirement: Create one response object containing method, endpoint, status, headers, and body.

stepLadder.title: Classify the status
stepLadder.requirement: Keep the response object and add one function that classifies the status as success, client error, or server error.

stepLadder.title: Read the content type
stepLadder.requirement: Keep all previous code and derive the content type from the response headers.

stepLadder.title: Summarize the JSON body
stepLadder.requirement: Add one focused function that summarizes the response body without changing earlier behavior.

stepLadder.title: Print the inspection report
stepLadder.requirement: Keep the entire solution and print one readable report containing endpoint, status classification, content type, and body summary.

modules.title: Build Read APIs with Node.js and Express
modules.purpose: Turn HTTP concepts into a running local Express service with focused GET routes.
learningObjectives: Start a local Express server.
Return JSON from GET routes.
Use route parameters for identity and query parameters for filtering.
Trace middleware and request flow.
guidedExercises: Start from one route before adding a collection.
Use localhost requests to inspect status and JSON output.
Keep lookup, filtering, and response construction focused.

sections.title: Express Read Routes
sections.summary: Build and query a deterministic local JSON API.

topics.title: Your First Node.js and Express Server
topics.summary: Start a local Express application, listen on a provided port, and return the first HTTP response.
learningGoals: Explain the role of Node.js in running server-side JavaScript.
Create an Express application and start the local server.
Return a simple response from a route handler.

topics.title: GET Routes and JSON Responses
topics.summary: Create read-only routes that return predictable JSON resources and collections.
learningGoals: Define GET routes for a collection and a single resource.
Return JSON with an explicit successful status.
Keep route handlers focused on one responsibility.

topics.title: Route Parameters and Query Parameters
topics.summary: Read path parameters for resource identity and query parameters for optional filtering.
learningGoals: Read an id from a route parameter.
Read optional filters from the query string.
Return 404 when a requested resource does not exist.

topics.title: Express Middleware and Request Flow
topics.summary: Use built-in middleware and trace how a request moves through parsing, routing, and response handling.
learningGoals: Use express.json when JSON request parsing is required.
Explain middleware order at a beginner level.
Keep request parsing separate from resource lookup and response construction.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Combine server startup, GET routes, ids, filters, and 404 behavior.

topics.title: Build a Read-Only Events API
topics.summary: Create an Express service that lists events, finds one event by id, and filters the collection with a query parameter.
learningGoals: Serve an in-memory event collection through Express.
Implement collection and resource GET routes.
Use route and query parameters predictably.

projectBrief.scenario: A campus website needs a local events service that frontend code can read without knowing how the event data is stored.
projectBrief.role: Junior backend developer responsible for the read side of the events API.
projectBrief.workspace: A local Node.js workspace with server.js, package.json, terminal access, and deterministic localhost HTTP requests. Express is provided by the course environment; learners do not install packages or call public APIs.
projectBrief.deliverable: A local Express API with GET /api/events, GET /api/events/:id, and category filtering.
requirements: Use only local in-memory event data; no database or public network is required.
Return JSON consistently.
Use meaningful status codes, including 404 for a missing event.
Preserve every working route while adding the next responsibility.

stepLadder.title: Create the Express application
stepLadder.requirement: Create the app and server startup using the provided local port contract.

stepLadder.title: Store the event collection
stepLadder.requirement: Add an in-memory events array with several consistently shaped event objects.

stepLadder.title: List all events
stepLadder.requirement: Add GET /api/events returning the complete collection as JSON.

stepLadder.title: Find one event by id
stepLadder.requirement: Add GET /api/events/:id and locate the matching event.

stepLadder.title: Handle a missing event
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve the route and return a 404 JSON response when the id is not found.

stepLadder.title: Read a category filter
stepLadder.requirement: Extend GET /api/events to read an optional category query parameter.

stepLadder.title: Filter without changing source data
stepLadder.requirement: Return only matching events when category is supplied while preserving the original collection.

stepLadder.title: Verify the read API
stepLadder.requirement: Keep the complete server and verify the collection, resource, missing-resource, and filter responses through localhost requests.

modules.title: Write Routes, Validation, and Errors
modules.purpose: Add controlled resource mutations while protecting the API contract from invalid input and missing resources.
learningObjectives: Create resources with POST.
Partially update resources with PATCH.
Delete resources intentionally.
Validate client input and return consistent errors.
guidedExercises: Preserve read routes while adding write behavior.
Compare client errors with unexpected server failures.

sections.title: Mutations and Error Contracts
sections.summary: Create, update, and delete resources without sacrificing predictable behavior.

topics.title: POST JSON and Create Resources
topics.summary: Accept a JSON request body, validate the required fields, create a resource, and return the created representation.
learningGoals: Read parsed JSON from req.body.
Validate required fields before creating a resource.
Return 201 with the created resource.

topics.title: PATCH and DELETE Resources
topics.summary: Update only supplied fields with PATCH and remove a resource with DELETE while handling missing ids.
learningGoals: Use PATCH for a partial resource update.
Use DELETE for resource removal.
Return appropriate success and not-found statuses.

topics.title: Validation and Client Errors
topics.summary: Reject malformed client input with consistent 400 responses and clear field-level messages.
learningGoals: Separate validation decisions from mutation.
Return 400 for invalid request data.
Use a predictable JSON error shape.

topics.title: Server Errors and Consistent API Responses
topics.summary: Handle unexpected failures without leaking implementation details and keep success/error response shapes understandable.
learningGoals: Distinguish expected client errors from unexpected server failures.
Return a safe 500 response for unexpected failures.
Use consistent response conventions across routes.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Extend the Events API into a validated local CRUD service.

topics.title: Build a Writable Events API
topics.summary: Extend an Express events service with create, update, delete, validation, and consistent error responses.
learningGoals: Create resources with POST.
Partially update resources with PATCH.
Delete resources and preserve clear error behavior.

projectBrief.scenario: The campus events team can now read events, but staff also need a controlled API for creating, editing, and removing event records.
projectBrief.role: Junior backend developer responsible for safe event mutations and client-facing validation.
projectBrief.workspace: A local Node.js workspace with server.js, package.json, terminal access, and deterministic localhost HTTP requests. Express is provided by the course environment; learners do not install packages or call public APIs.
projectBrief.deliverable: A CRUD-style local Events API with POST, PATCH, DELETE, validation, and consistent errors.
requirements: Keep the existing read routes working.
Validate client input before mutating the in-memory collection.
Use 201, 400, 404, and successful delete/update responses intentionally.
Do not add authentication, a database, or deployment yet.

stepLadder.title: Enable JSON request parsing
stepLadder.requirement: Add the Express JSON middleware required by write routes.

stepLadder.title: Validate new event input
stepLadder.requirement: Add one focused validation function for the required event fields.

stepLadder.title: Create an event
stepLadder.requirement: Add POST /api/events and append one valid event with a generated local id.

stepLadder.title: Return created status
stepLadder.requirement: Return the created event with HTTP 201 without changing the read routes.

stepLadder.title: Reject invalid creates
stepLadder.requirement: Return a consistent 400 JSON error when required fields are missing or invalid.

stepLadder.title: Find an event for updates
stepLadder.requirement: Add the resource lookup needed by PATCH /api/events/:id.

stepLadder.title: Patch supplied fields
stepLadder.requirement: Update only allowed fields that were supplied in the request body.

stepLadder.title: Delete an event
stepLadder.requirement: Add DELETE /api/events/:id and remove the matching resource.

stepLadder.title: Handle missing mutation targets
stepLadder.requirement: Return a consistent 404 response from PATCH and DELETE when the id does not exist.

stepLadder.title: Verify the complete writable API
stepLadder.requirement: Exercise create, invalid create, patch, delete, and missing-resource behavior against localhost.

modules.title: Persist APIs with SQLite
modules.purpose: Replace temporary in-memory state with a local relational database while preserving a clean HTTP contract.
learningObjectives: Persist API resources in SQLite.
Use parameterized SQL from Node.js.
Separate repository/database responsibilities from Express routes.
Preserve API behavior across server restarts.
guidedExercises: Create and inspect a local SQLite database inside the learner workspace.
Use prepared statements rather than interpolating client input into SQL.
Replace one in-memory operation at a time so HTTP behavior stays stable.

sections.title: SQLite Persistence
sections.summary: Connect Express routes to a local SQLite database through focused data-access code.

topics.title: SQLite Persistence for APIs
topics.summary: Replace temporary in-memory data with a local SQLite database that survives server restarts.
learningGoals: Explain why in-memory arrays lose data when a server restarts.
Open a local SQLite database from Node.js.
Create a small events table with stable columns and constraints.

topics.title: Parameterized SQL from Node.js
topics.summary: Use prepared statements and parameters so API input becomes safe database queries instead of string-built SQL.
learningGoals: Prepare SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements from Node.js.
Bind values with parameters instead of concatenating user input.
Map database rows to predictable JSON resources.

topics.title: Repository Layer and Persistent CRUD
topics.summary: Move database access behind focused repository functions so Express routes stay about HTTP.
learningGoals: Separate route handling from database access.
Implement persistent event lookup, creation, update, and deletion.
Preserve API status/error behavior while changing the storage layer.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Replace in-memory event storage with durable SQLite persistence.

topics.title: Build a Database-Backed Events API
topics.summary: Replace the Events API in-memory collection with SQLite while preserving the existing HTTP contract.
learningGoals: Create and initialize the events database.
Move CRUD operations into repository functions.
Keep the Express routes stable while persistence changes underneath.

projectBrief.scenario: The campus Events API works, but every restart loses the event data. The team needs local persistent storage without changing the frontend-facing API contract.
projectBrief.role: Backend developer responsible for adding persistence behind an existing HTTP API.
projectBrief.workspace: A local Node.js workspace with Express, curl, SQLite, terminal access, and deterministic localhost HTTP requests. Course dependencies are pre-provisioned by Zoéskoul; learners do not install packages.
projectBrief.deliverable: A local Express Events API whose CRUD operations persist to data/events.db.
requirements: Use the course-provided Node.js, Express, SQLite, and curl tooling.
Keep external network access disabled.
Use parameterized SQL for values supplied by clients.
Keep SQL/database logic out of route handlers where practical.
Preserve the existing GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, validation, and error contracts.

stepLadder.title: Create the database module
stepLadder.requirement: Open data/events.db and create the events table when it does not exist.

stepLadder.title: Seed deterministic starting events
stepLadder.requirement: Insert the provided starter rows only when the table is empty.

stepLadder.title: Read all events from SQLite
stepLadder.requirement: Replace the in-memory collection read with a parameterized database query.

stepLadder.title: Read one event by id
stepLadder.requirement: Query one event by id and preserve the existing 404 behavior.

stepLadder.title: Create a persistent event
stepLadder.requirement: Insert a validated event and return the stored row with 201.

stepLadder.title: Patch a persistent event
stepLadder.requirement: Update allowed supplied fields without replacing unspecified values.

stepLadder.title: Delete a persistent event
stepLadder.requirement: Delete the target row and preserve missing-resource behavior.

stepLadder.title: Extract repository functions
stepLadder.requirement: Keep SQL/database access in focused repository functions used by the routes.

stepLadder.title: Verify persistence
stepLadder.requirement: Create data, restart the server, and confirm the event remains available.

stepLadder.title: Verify the complete contract
stepLadder.requirement: Use localhost requests to verify read, filter, create, invalid create, patch, delete, and 404 behavior.

modules.title: Final Capstone: Campus Events API
modules.purpose: Integrate HTTP, Express, validation, error handling, and SQLite persistence into one coherent local API service.
learningObjectives: Design a coherent REST-style event resource contract.
Implement read and write routes cumulatively.
Apply validation and predictable status/error behavior.
Verify the complete API locally.
guidedExercises: Trace the complete contract before implementation.
Preserve all working routes as capabilities are added.
Verify each HTTP outcome through localhost.
modules.moduleProject: Build and verify the Campus Events API.

sections.title: Final Capstone
sections.summary: Build the complete persistent Campus Events API with Express and SQLite.

topics.title: Final Capstone: Build the Campus Events API
topics.summary: Build a complete local Express API for campus events with SQLite persistence, read routes, filters, mutations, validation, and resilient error responses.
learningGoals: Design and implement a coherent REST-style resource API.
Preserve predictable JSON contracts across read and write routes.
Persist event resources in SQLite through focused repository functions.
Validate client input and distinguish 400, 404, and 500 outcomes.
Verify the API through deterministic localhost requests.

projectBrief.scenario: The Campus Event Explorer is ready for a real backend boundary. Build the local service that could power its event list, filters, detail views, and staff updates.
projectBrief.role: API developer responsible for the complete HTTP contract and Express implementation.
projectBrief.workspace: A local Node.js workspace with server.js, package.json, terminal access, and deterministic localhost HTTP requests. Express is provided by the course environment; learners do not install packages or call public APIs.
projectBrief.deliverable: A complete persistent Campus Events API with GET collection/resource routes, filtering, POST, PATCH, DELETE, validation, SQLite persistence, and consistent success/error responses.
requirements: Use JavaScript, Node.js, Express, and local SQLite only.
Keep API behavior deterministic and testable on 127.0.0.1.
Use parameterized SQL for client-supplied database values.
Keep route, validation, and repository responsibilities understandable.
Build cumulatively so each step begins with the complete previous solution.
Do not introduce authentication, deployment, TypeScript, hosted databases, or frontend frameworks.

stepLadder.title: Create the server shell
stepLadder.requirement: Create the Express app, JSON middleware, and local server startup contract.

stepLadder.title: Model the event resource
stepLadder.requirement: Add a small in-memory collection whose event objects share one documented shape.

stepLadder.title: List events
stepLadder.requirement: Implement GET /api/events with a predictable JSON collection response.

stepLadder.title: Filter events
stepLadder.requirement: Extend the collection route with an optional category query filter.

stepLadder.title: Read one event
stepLadder.requirement: Implement GET /api/events/:id for a matching resource.

stepLadder.title: Handle missing reads
stepLadder.requirement: Return a consistent 404 JSON error when a requested event is absent.

stepLadder.title: Validate event input
stepLadder.requirement: Add one reusable validator for fields accepted by create and update operations.

stepLadder.title: Create events
stepLadder.requirement: Implement POST /api/events and return the created resource with 201.

stepLadder.title: Reject invalid creates
stepLadder.requirement: Return a consistent 400 response without mutating data when create input is invalid.

stepLadder.title: Patch events
stepLadder.requirement: Implement PATCH /api/events/:id so only allowed supplied fields change.

stepLadder.title: Delete events
stepLadder.requirement: Implement DELETE /api/events/:id while preserving all read and update behavior.

stepLadder.title: Unify client errors
stepLadder.requirement: Make 400 and 404 responses follow one understandable JSON error convention.

stepLadder.title: Persist events with SQLite
stepLadder.requirement: Replace temporary in-memory event storage with repository functions backed by data/events.db.

stepLadder.title: Handle unexpected failures
stepLadder.requirement: Add a final safe error handler that returns 500 without exposing internal details.

stepLadder.title: Verify the complete contract
stepLadder.requirement: Run deterministic localhost checks for list, filter, detail, create, invalid input, patch, delete, 404, and error response behavior.
